title: Influence of Electrostatic Environment on the Proximity Spin-Orbit Coupling in Graphene on Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Bert Jorissen, Bart Partoens, Aires Ferreira, Lucian Covaci
abstract: We investigate the proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in graphene on transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures using a tight-binding approach. The tight-binding parameters of an effective 4-band model describing the low-energy physics of the graphene layer are extracted as a function of twist angle, material composition (MoS${}_2$, MoSe${}_2$, WS${}_2$, WSe${}_2$), band alignment, and charge-transfer dipole. We investigate the effect of a charge-transfer dipole induced on the chalcogen layer closest to graphene, which is typically neglected in tight-binding models but included in ab initio calculations through charge redistribution. In addition, we explore the influence of variations in the band alignment. We find that the spin-valley and Rashba spin-orbit coupling energies as well as the so-called Rashba phase, governing the orientation of momentum-space spin textures, show a strong dependence on the twist angle and electrostatic tuning. Our results suggest that variations in band alignment and charge redistribution contribute to the spread of spin-orbit parameters reported in the literature.
summary: This theoretical study models the proximity spin-orbit coupling in graphene placed on TMDs using a tight-binding approach. By systematically varying the twist angle and incorporating the effects of charge-transfer dipoles and band alignment, the authors demonstrate that these electrostatic factors critically govern the resulting SOC parameters. The work provides a framework to reconcile discrepancies in the literature regarding these crucial quantum material properties.
main_problem: The study investigates how the local electrostatic environment influences the proximity-induced spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in graphene when placed on transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) heterostructures.
main_result: The SOC parameters, including spin-valley and Rashba terms, are strongly dependent on the twist angle and electrostatic tuning, suggesting that band alignment variations are key contributors to discrepancies in existing literature.
method: The authors employ a tight-binding (TB) approach using an effective 4-band model for graphene coupled to a full TMD model, systematically varying parameters like twist angle and charge-transfer dipoles.
model_or_system: The system is a graphene/TMD heterostructure (e.g., MoS2, WSe2). The model uses a full TB Hamiltonian incorporating graphene, TMD, and interlayer coupling terms, which is then reduced to an effective model to capture proximity-induced SOC effects.
key_observables: Spin-valley (SV) and Rashba (R) SOC energies, the Rashba phase ($\varphi_R$), and the spin-orbit gap.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), material composition ($	ext{MoS}_2, 	ext{MoSe}_2$, etc.), band alignment ($E_C, E_V$), and charge-transfer dipole strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis isolates the effects of the charge-transfer dipole and band alignment, treating the dipole as a minimal interface on-site correction.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the supercell structure for a twisted graphene/MoS2 configuration. Other figures likely compare band structures derived from the full and effective TB models.
paper_structure: The paper systematically constructs and analyzes a full TB model for the heterostructure, derives an effective low-energy model for graphene, and then analyzes the dependence of key SOC parameters on external electrostatic tuning and structural parameters.
why_interesting: The explicit theoretical modeling of proximity effects in 2D heterostructures, particularly linking band alignment and interface dipoles to fundamental symmetries like the Rashba phase, is highly relevant for designing quantum materials for spintronics and topological quantum computing.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The supercell for a twisted graphene/MoS2 configuration with (7,−5,4,−5) and θ = 9.17◦, ε = −3.28%. The orange and red sites indicate the graphene A and B sublattices, whereas the blue and yellow sites indicate the TMD metal (Mo) and chalcogen (S) sites.

Figure 2: (left) The side view of the two layers in the heterostructure, with the rel- evant interlayer hoppings and distances indicated. (right) Schematic of the band alignment of the graphene Dirac cone in the TMD band gap.

Figure 3: (left) Low-energy bands of the full (solid) and effective (dotted) TB model for MoS2 with (7,−5,4,−5) as shown in Figure 1, with θ = 9.17◦, ε = −3.28% and EC = 0.04 eV. The fitted parameters are λSV = 0.35 meV, λR = 0.21 meV, φR = −1.24 rad and ϵλ = 13.29. (right) Spin expectation values for the low-energy bands. The k-path and first Brillouin zone are indicated in the inset to the middle panel.

Figure 4: The SOC parameters for MoS2, without dipole, with E0 C = 0.04 eV offset. The cross indicates the configuration shown in Figure 3. The harmonic fit is indicated with a dotted line. The colour and size of the dots correspond to the strain applied (larger dots indicate less strained structures). The results from Li and Koshino [63] are indicated by the dashed lines on the left panel (note that they used a different band alignment fb and methodology).

Figure 5: Changes to the SOC parameters with the tuning of the dipole, with the reference EC as given in Table 1 for MoS2. Changing the dipole does not produce significant changes in the parameters. The configuration from Figure 3 and the dipole of δNCT = 0e and +0.1e are indicated with a cross and dotted lines, respectively.
